html:
The Province of Quebec was the British colony made from French Canada after Britain won it in the Seven Years' War. It lasted from 1763 to 1791. The map shows it in 1783, stretching from the Gulf of St. Lawrence to the Great Lakes, and in 1800, when its core had become Lower Canada.

Its people were mostly French-speaking Catholics, the heirs of New France. In the Quebec Act of 1774 Britain let them keep their religion and French civil law, and stretched the province south to the Ohio River. The American colonists saw this as a threat, and their army invaded in 1775 but failed to take Quebec City.

After 1783 the Loyalists who settled upstream wanted English law. The Constitutional Act of 1791 split the province in two: English-speaking Upper Canada, now Ontario, and French-speaking Lower Canada, now Quebec. Both became part of Canada in 1867.
